conceptZh: 臉上用來呼吸和聞味道的器官。
object: a chunky toy warrior with foam sword, a gachapon capsule, and a springy cartoon elephant trunk
morph: a capsule pops open and pieces of 鼻 burst out in a surprise
creativeAngle: 玩具戰士打開扭蛋，裡面彈出字的各部分；最後大象鼻孔噴出氣球。
promptEn: An 8-second silly animated clip, bright pastel look, soft daylight, no dark grading. On a lime-green and cream toy arena floor, a chunky toy warrior with a foam sword and round shield eyes a giant orange capsule with grim bravado. 0–1.6s: He pokes the capsule with the sword as the first 鼻 is spoken; the capsule pops open and the top piece 自 bursts out and clangs on his shield; he does a huge double-take. 1.6–3.2s: The second 鼻 is spoken as a second capsule hatches the middle part, bouncing off his helmet and rolling past his boots; he hides behind the shield. 3.2–4.8s: A third capsule cracks open and the bottom 畀 piece springs up, and all pieces snap into 鼻 in rich crimson as the warrior flips backward. 4.8–5.8s: As 鼻孔 is spoken, a toy elephant pops out of the last capsule and its trunk tip, with two round nostrils, puffs a pair of tiny confetti clouds, and the warrior salutes. Final hold (about 5.0–8.0s): the elephant sways its trunk and the warrior waves his sword; the glyph is still. Narration: one gentle off-screen voice, Taiwan standard Mandarin, speaks only this line and nothing else, each syllable clear with its tone: 鼻、鼻、鼻孔（ㄅㄧˊ、ㄅㄧˊ、ㄅㄧˊ ㄎㄨㄥˇ）. The first 鼻 lands at about 1.0s, the second 鼻 at about 2.6s, and the word 鼻孔 at about 4.9s, each timed to the picture described above. On-screen text is limited to the one glyph 鼻 in strong solid color over a light bright background; the spoken word is never shown as text. The glyph 鼻 fills roughly 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped, and stays perfectly still for the final 3 seconds while the lead keeps playing away from the strokes. No real people, no flashing.

conceptZh: 臉上用來呼吸和聞味道的器官。
object: a chunky wind-up toy shark loaded onto a toy springboard catapult, aimed at a giant squeaky rubber nose on a pedestal, with a tower of crimson foam blocks behind it
morph: the shark is launched, sails right past the rubber nose, BONKS into the foam-block tower and lands upside-down in a bucket; the knocked-loose blocks tumble down and settle as the three stacked parts of 鼻: 自 on top, 田 in the middle, 丌 at the bottom
creativeAngle: 改用「發射」橋段：發條鯊魚被橡膠恐龍用大腳踩彈板彈飛，想咬大橡膠鼻子卻整個飛過頭，撞倒後方積木塔，倒栽進水桶。撞擊震落的積木自己疊成「鼻」，上自、中田、下丌結構清楚。和前一版（戰士開膠囊）完全不同，動作連續、每1.5秒有新事件，單字「鼻子」配合大橡膠鼻子按壓叫聲出現。
promptEn:
An 8-second slapstick animated clip, bright pastel toy-arena look, soft even daylight, no dark grading. Cream floor, pale sky-blue backdrop, nothing busy behind. Cast: a chunky wind-up toy shark with a big goofy grin, a turning key on its back and jaws that chomp at everything (it always bites the wrong thing, then spins in a circle on dry land), and a rubber dinosaur with enormous feet and comically tiny arms that cannot reach anything. Props: a toy springboard catapult on the left, a giant squeaky rubber nose on a short pedestal in the middle, a tower of crimson foam blocks on the right, and a small bucket at the far right edge.

0–1.5s: The shark sits on the catapult plate, eyes locked on the giant rubber nose, jaws chomping hungrily at the air. The dinosaur tries to push the shark forward with its tiny arms, cannot reach, shrugs. The first 鼻 is spoken at about 1.0s as the shark points its snout straight at the rubber nose.
1.5–3.0s: The dinosaur backs up, does a drumroll shuffle with its huge feet, then STOMPS the far end of the springboard with its whole body. The shark is launched in a huge arc across the frame, jaws snapping at empty air as it sails right over the rubber nose, missing it completely.
3.0–4.5s: BONK! The shark slams face-first into the crimson foam-block tower with cartoon squash-and-stretch, ricochets off, and drops upside-down into the bucket, tail wiggling out the top. The tower collapses: blocks tumble down and settle neatly center-frame as the glyph 鼻 in rich crimson, upper part 自 on top, 田 in the middle, 丌 at the bottom, every stroke correct. The second 鼻 is spoken at about 4.4s exactly as the last block clicks into place.
4.5–8.0s: The glyph 鼻 holds perfectly still, centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with clean margins. At about 5.2s the word 鼻子 is spoken: the dinosaur, still unable to reach with its tiny arms, bumps the giant rubber nose with its whole snout; the nose squashes, honks and bounces back up, wiggling. Away from the strokes, the shark pops out of the bucket with a dazed happy grin and spins in a slow circle on its belly, then gives a tiny tail-wag victory pose as the clip ends. Nobody is hurt, no loud startling sounds.

Narration: one warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua) speaks only this line and nothing else, slowly and distinctly, each syllable with its clear tone: 鼻、鼻、鼻子（ㄅㄧˊ、ㄅㄧˊ、ㄅㄧˊ ˙ㄗ）. Read exactly those syllables and stop after the word; do not repeat the line. Soft toy-arena sound effects (boing, bonk, squeak) stay quieter than the voice. On-screen text is limited to the single glyph 鼻 in solid crimson over the light background; the spoken word is never shown as text, no subtitles, no watermark, no flashing. No real people, no realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toy figures.

conceptZh: 桶子身材的玩具海盜聞到高柱頂上的派香味，鼻子一抽一抽地把紅木箱越疊越高，不肯幫忙的鸚鵡偏偏落在塔頂最後一格，整座箱塔轟然倒下摔成「鼻」字，海盜被埋得只露出眼睛和鼻子，鸚鵡就得意地站上他的鼻子。
object: a wobbling tower of glossy crimson toy treasure crates stacked by a barrel-shaped toy pirate chasing the smell of a golden pie
morph: the overloaded crate tower topples and the tumbling crimson crates land center-frame in three clear tiers — 自 on top, 田 in the middle, 丌 at the bottom — forming one correctly structured, still 鼻
creativeAngle: 之前幾版是膠囊蹦出零件和鯊魚撞塔，這次改成「疊高再倒塌」：整個笑點都從「鼻子」來，海盜靠鼻子聞香才開始疊箱子，倒下的箱子分成自、田、丌三層落下，部件看得很清楚；最後鸚鵡站在海盜露出來的鼻子上，剛好在說「鼻子」的時候，聽到的和看到的是同一件事。不用披風英雄，畫面上只放海盜、鸚鵡和箱子，比較好看懂。
promptEn:
An 8-second slapstick animated clip, bright pastel toy-playset look, soft even daylight, no dark grading. Pale butter-yellow floor, light sky-blue backdrop, nothing busy behind. Lead: a round barrel-shaped toy pirate with a tiny tricorn hat, a painted eyepatch and a big red bulb nose that twitches at every smell. His sidekick is a plump green toy parrot that flatly refuses to help: it folds its wings, turns its back and always lands in the worst possible spot. On the right stands a tall thin post with a steaming golden pie on top.

0–1.6s: The pirate's nose twitches, he sniffs the air and stretches toward the pie, then points up at it, licking his lips. As the first 鼻 is spoken (about 1.0s) he slams down the first glossy crimson crate and hops on top.
1.6–3.2s: Faster and faster he stacks more crimson crates and climbs, wobbling on tiptoe, and the tower sways wider with every crate. He waves at the parrot for help; the parrot turns away and pretends to look at its claws.
3.2–4.4s: The pirate's fingertips are a hair from the pie. The parrot hops onto the very top crate, the tiniest extra weight. Everything freezes for one beat as the pirate's eyes go wide. Then the tower tips and comes down in a huge tumbling crash. The crates land center-frame in three clear tiers and settle as the glyph 鼻 in solid crimson: 自 on top, 田 in the middle, 丌 at the bottom, every stroke correctly formed. The second 鼻 is spoken (about 4.4s) as the last crate clicks into place.
4.4–8.0s: The glyph 鼻 holds perfectly still, centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with clean margins. In the lower-left corner, clear of the strokes, the pirate lies buried in a small heap of gold coins with only his blinking eyes and red bulb nose poking out. As the word 鼻子 is spoken (about 5.4s), the parrot flutters down and plants itself smugly right on top of his nose. The nose squashes, wiggles and gives a soft honk, the pirate goes cross-eyed with a dizzy happy grin, and the pie flops gently onto his hat. Cartoon bonks only, nobody hurt.

Narration: one warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua) reads only these exact syllables, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops: 鼻、鼻、鼻子（ㄅㄧˊ、ㄅㄧˊ、ㄅㄧˊ ˙ㄗ）. No other speech. Soft sound effects (thunk, wobble creak, crash, honk) stay quieter than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single glyph 鼻. No subtitles, no watermark, no flashing. All characters are stylized toys; no real people or realistic human figures.
